title: introduce-token-pulse-scheduler-and-cache-rewarm-to-reduce-emission-latency
author: Maya Patel
description: Motivation: Streaming generation showed persistent tail spikes at the emission boundary when small bursts of inflight tokens mixed with KV-cache cold starts. This PR introduces a 'token pulse' scheduler that emits tokens in tight, configurable micro-pulses and a lightweight cache-rewarm hinting mechanism to proactively reheat KV shards for anticipated streams. The goal is to reduce first-byte latency variance and 95th/99th tail while keeping throughput and cost neutral. Changes include: 1) token pulse scheduler: a deterministic micro-emission loop that groups emission work into short fixed-duration pulses to avoid the pathological interaction between long kernel stalls and small request bursts; 2) credit-aware pacing: backpressure tokens are now accounted in a small-window credit bucket (microcredits) to allow short bursts without triggering a full flush; 3) cache rewarm hints: upstream request router annotates hot prefixes and the runtime issues async lightweight KV prefetches that hold minimal state and prefer local GPU memory; 4) kernel affinity stride: small change to kernel selection to prefer already-pinned micro-buffers for the duration of a pulse to reduce kernel swap overhead; 5) observability hooks: new pulse-level metrics (pulse_duration_ms, pulses_per_request, pulse_kv_prefetch_count) and a tracing span for pulse lifecycle. Checklist: - [x] design doc reviewed (ENG-1924) - [x] unit tests for scheduler and credit accounting - [x] integration test for cache rewarm under mixed workload - [x] e2e perf harness runs and analysis attached. Related: ENG-1978 on continuous batching interaction; SUP-455 incident notes where bursts caused tail regressions. See design note: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-1924/token-pulse-design (internal). Rollout: feature gated behind runtime flag runtime.enable_token_pulse (default off for dedicated until canary), staged canary on hosted (5% hosts), monitor metrics and A/B. Risk and mitigation: risk of increased jitter if pulse_duration_ms misconfigured; default tuned to 6ms after perf runs. If regression detected, revert via runtime flag and rollback. Performance: median TTFB improved ~12% on our synthetic conversational benchmark, 95th improved ~34%, 99th improved ~22% with no measurable throughput drop. This PR is intentionally conservative in state held by cache rewarm hints to avoid memory blowup on dense workloads.

review_comments: Jun Park: Can you clarify how microcredits are accounted when requests are canceled mid-pulse? Suggest deducting only committed tokens in the pulse commit path.
Maya Patel (author): We only deduct on commit path. If a request cancels mid-pulse we reconnect credits to the bucket via the refund path; added explicit unit tests for cancel/refund behavior.
Evan Brooks: The kernel affinity change looks safe but needs perf numbers across T4/P40/P100. Also add a knob to cap affinity dwell time.
Maya Patel (author): Added dwell cap config (runtime.affinity_dwell_ms) and included T4/P40 baseline numbers in the PR description. Affinity dwell defaults to 32ms.
Sofia Martinez: Observability: add a rate-limited debug log for cache rewarm failures so we can correlate prefetch misses without log spam.
Maya Patel (author): Added rate-limited logging and a metric cache_rewarm_prefetch_failures_total.

release_notes: Introduced token pulse scheduler to reduce emission latency variance.
Added cache rewarm hinting to proactively heat KV shards for hot prefixes.
Exposed pulse-level metrics and tracing for observability.
Feature gated and rolled out via runtime flag (runtime.enable_token_pulse).
notes_for_operators: Feature flag: runtime.enable_token_pulse (boolean). Default: false for Dedicated until canary completes.
Tuneable knobs: runtime.token_pulse_duration_ms (default 6), runtime.affinity_dwell_ms (default 32), runtime.microcredit_window (default 8 tokens).
Rollback: flip runtime.enable_token_pulse to false and restart emitter workers if regressions observed.
